    Texas Legislature
    Governing body
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The Texas House of Representatives is the lower chamber of the Texas Legislature, comprised of 150 members elected from single-member districts for two-year terms. As of 2025, Republicans hold a majority with 88 seats. The chamber convenes at the Texas Capitol in Austin and is currently led by Speaker Dustin Burrows (as of 2026). 
    Key Details 
    • Composition: 150 members, no term limits.
    • Leadership: Speaker Dustin Burrows (serving since 2025).
    • Location: Texas State Capitol, Austin.
    • Partisan Breakdown (2025): 88 Republicans, 62 Democrats.
    • Functions: Passes legislation, sets state budget, and initiates articles of impeachment. 
    Key Information & Resources 
    • Find Your Representative: Use the official Who Represents Me? website to find representatives by address.
    • Contact Information: A directory of members and their capitol office numbers can be found through the Texas House of Representatives website.
    • Legislative Information: Information on bills, committee schedules, and live broadcasts of house sessions is available on the official House website. 
    Qualifications for Membership 
    • Must be a citizen of the United States.
    • Must be a qualified elector of the State of Texas.
    • Must be at least 21 years old.
    • Must have lived in Texas for at least two years, and the last year in the district they are representing. 
    The Texas House operates during regular sessions, which convene on the second Tuesday of January in odd-numbered years, though special sessions can be called by the Governor.

    Contact Information. How to contact a member of the Texas House of Representatives?
    About this result
    Feedback
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    To contact a Texas House of Representatives member, use the "Who Represents Me" tool on the Texas Legislature Online (TLO) website to find your representative by address. Contact them via email (using their member page form), by phone at their district office, or by writing to: The Honorable [Name], Texas House of Representatives, P.O. Box 2910, Austin, Texas 78768-2910. 
    Key Methods to Contact Members
    • Find Your Representative: Use the official "Who Represents Me?" site to get the exact phone number, email address, and office location for your representative. 
    • Email: Members often provide email contact forms on their personal pages within the Texas House website. 
    • Phone: You can find the number for their Capitol office or local district office via the Texas Legislature Online directory. 
    • Mail: Use the official mailing address provided for the Capitol building. 
    • Social Media: Many representatives are accessible through their official Facebook or Twitter/X accounts.
    Tips for Effective Communication
    • Identify Yourself as a Constituent: State that you live in their district to ensure your voice is heard. 
    • Be Specific: Focus on one topic or bill number per message.
    • Be Professional: Write a concise, courteous message. 
    When contacting them, keep in mind that personalized messages (emails or letters) are generally more effective than form letters.

      Member Qualifications. What are the qualifications to be a member of the Texas House of Representatives?
      About this result
      Feedback
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      To be a member of the Texas House of Representatives, a person must be a U.S. citizen, at least 21 years old, a qualified elector of the state, a Texas resident for two years, and a resident of their district for one year. They serve two-year terms with no term limits. 
      Qualifications for Texas House of Representatives
      • Citizenship: Must be a citizen of the United States. 
      • Age: Must be at least 21 years old. 
      • Residency (State): Must have been a resident of Texas for at least two years prior to election. 
      • Residency (District): Must have been a resident of the district they represent for at least one year. 
      • Voter Eligibility: Must be a qualified elector (registered voter) of the state. 
      Usage Examples / Contextual Requirements 
      • Term Limits: There are no term limits for Texas Representatives.
      • Term Length: Members serve two-year terms.
      • Legislative Body: The House is composed of 150 members.
      • Role: Representative of a single-member district.
      Synonyms of Qualifications Requirements, Eligibility criteria, Conditions for office, Prerequisites, and Legislative eligibility.
      Note: The qualifications above are for the Texas House of Representatives (state level). Do not confuse these with the requirements for the U.S. House of Representatives.

        Bill Passing Process. What is the process for passing a bill in the Texas House of Representatives?
        About this result
        Feedback
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        Passing a bill in the Texas House involves filing by a member, committee review/report, scheduling by the Calendars Committee, and three readings with debate/voting (simple majority typically needed). The bill must then pass the Senate and be signed by the Governor, or it dies, with the process operating within a 140-day biennial session. 
        Key Stages in the Texas House
        • Filing & First Reading:
          A Representative files the bill, which is read and referred to a committee. 
        • Committee Action:
          The committee hears testimony, holds markup sessions, and votes to report the bill favorably, favorably with changes, or not at all. 
        • Calendars Committee:
          If approved by the committee, the bill is scheduled for debate by the Calendars Committee. 
        • Floor Action:
          • Second Reading: The bill is debated, amended, and tentatively voted on. 
          • Third Reading: The bill is read again, allowing for final amendments and a final vote. 
        • Engrossment:
          Once passed on third reading, the bill is sent to the Senate. 
        Synonyms/Related Terms for the Process Legislative process, How a bill becomes law, Bill progression, and House proceedings.
        Key Rules & Considerations
        • Session Limits:
          The legislature meets for only 140 days every two years. 
        • Reading Requirements:
          Bills are traditionally read on three separate days, though this can be suspended. 
        • Vote Thresholds:
          A simple majority is required, but a four-fifths vote can suspend reading rules. 
        • End Goal:
          The bill must pass both chambers in identical form before reaching the Governor's desk.
